description: Workforce-of-the-future grant-domain terminology. Covers WIOA, Registered Apprenticeship, sector partnerships, recognition-of-prior-learning, micro-credentials, and job-quality framing. Drawn from DOL ETA program guidance and the Good Jobs Initiative. Starter pack — extend with PA-specific DCED + L&I program detail as field experience accumulates.

domains.name: WIOA programs and titles
domains.description: Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act funding streams and target populations.

domains.name: Apprenticeship + credential frameworks
domains.description: Registered Apprenticeship, recognition-of-prior-learning, micro-credentials, stackable pathways.

domains.name: Outcome metrics + job-quality framing
domains.description: Median wage, retention, credential attainment — the metrics DOL reviewers actually score.

facts.statement: WIOA Title I has three funding streams: (1) Adult — workers 18+ with priority for low-income, public-assistance, basic-skills-deficient; (2) Dislocated Worker — laid-off / displaced incumbents, including long-term unemployed and trade-affected; (3) Youth — out-of-school 16-24 prioritized at 75% of funds, in-school 14-21 up to 25%. Local Workforce Development Boards administer; states pass through.

WIOA Title II funds adult education and family literacy (administered by ED, not DOL — common confusion). Title III is the Wagner-Peyser employment service (state ES offices). Title IV funds vocational rehabilitation. When a proposal references 'WIOA' generically, reviewers ask which Title — be specific. Title I + III braiding is the canonical workforce-services combination at One-Stop / American Job Centers.

Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) is DOL- or State-Apprenticeship-Agency-registered, requires 2000+ on-the-job hours, related technical instruction, progressive wage schedule, EEO compliance, ends in journey-worker credential. 'Apprenticeship-like,' 'pre-apprenticeship,' 'industry-recognized apprenticeship' (IRAP) are NOT RAP — DOL retired IRAP framework in 2022. Pre-apprenticeship is a feeder model with formal RAP partnership agreement. Cite the RAPIDS 671 program number when referencing a specific RAP.

DOL Sector Partnerships are industry-aligned, region-bounded employer collaboratives that drive workforce strategy for a specific sector (e.g., advanced manufacturing in the Lehigh Valley, healthcare in Western PA). Strong proposals identify the existing sector partnership, name the convener, list industry partners, and show employer commitment letters specifying hiring intent. Hiring intent should be: number of hires, position type, wage range, retention target.

Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) credits demonstrated competency from work experience, military service, or non-credit training toward a credential or degree. DOL-favored RPL methods: portfolio assessment, challenge exams, industry-certification crosswalk (e.g., MSSC CPT → 9 college credits). RPL framing reduces program length + cost — strong proposals quantify time-to-credential reduction and credit-bearing equivalency.

Stackable credentials = sequence of industry-recognized credentials that build progressively (e.g., CompTIA A+ → Net+ → Sec+). Micro-credentials are short, competency-specific (typically 40-200 hours of learning), often digital-badge-issued. DOL TAACCCT-era language preferred. Strong proposals show the credential-stack pathway (timeline + wage progression at each rung) rather than isolated credential listings.

WIOA Common Performance Measures (Title I/III/II/IV reportable): (1) Employment Rate Q2 after exit, (2) Employment Rate Q4 after exit, (3) Median Earnings Q2 after exit, (4) Credential Attainment Rate within 1 year of exit, (5) Measurable Skill Gains during program, (6) Effectiveness in Serving Employers. Strong proposals state baseline + target for each applicable measure; reviewers reject proposals that promise unrealistically high outcomes vs. local-workforce-board historical performance.

DOL Good Jobs Initiative defines job quality as: (1) recruitment + hiring (equitable + accessible), (2) benefits, (3) DEIA + accessibility, (4) empowerment + representation, (5) job security + working conditions, (6) organizational culture, (7) pay, (8) skills + career advancement. ETA + EDA + Commerce competitive grants increasingly require Good Jobs Principles compliance — frame employer commitments against these eight, not just wage.

WIOA defines 'individuals with barriers to employment' to include: low-income; basic-skills-deficient; long-term unemployed; ex-offenders; persons with disabilities; English language learners; low-literacy; homeless; foster youth aging out; pregnant or parenting youth; older workers (55+); single parents; veterans (especially disabled). Stacking 2+ barrier categories raises priority weight. Always quantify projected enrollment by barrier category in the proposal narrative.

'Earn-and-learn' is DOL-favored framing for paid-while-training models — apprenticeship, OJT (on-the-job training), incumbent worker training, work-based learning. Reviewers reward earn-and-learn over classroom-only because (1) participants don't choose between income and training, (2) employer-skin-in-game via wage payment, (3) higher completion rates. Proposals proposing classroom-only models should justify the choice or pivot framing.

Wage outcome claims in DOL-funded programs should specify: entry wage, post-credential wage at 1 year, post-credential wage at 3 years (or maximum window the program can credibly track). Self-sufficiency wage (region-specific, MIT Living Wage Calculator preferred over federal poverty-level) is the reviewer-expected benchmark for 'family-sustaining wage.' Avoid uncited 'living wage' claims without geographic specificity.

PA-specific workforce funding adjacencies: PA DCED Industry Partnerships ($), PA L&I PAsmart ($STEM-aligned), PAsmart Apprenticeship ($), Workforce Innovation Networks (WIN) regional grants. Federal-state braiding is reviewer-expected: PA proposals leveraging WIOA Title I + DCED Industry Partnership + private match score higher than single-source funding requests. Cite the specific PA PA Local Workforce Development Board (LWDB) by name.

relationships.description: Registered Apprenticeships at scale typically operate inside DOL Sector Partnerships — the partnership convenes employer demand, the RAP delivers structured training.
Stackable-credential pathways depend on RPL to give credit for already-demonstrated competency between rungs.
Good Jobs Principle 7 (pay) is operationalized via the wage-progression metric stack.
Barriers-to-employment categorization shapes how WIOA Common Performance Measures are reported (different baseline expectations for higher-barrier cohorts).
